classification_signals: The paper proposes a 'Biophilic Industrial Design Framework' (Section 5, Figure 15).
It introduces 'Further Criteria for Bio-Collaboration within Design Products' (Section 4.2) and applies them to existing industrial design examples (Sections 3.1, Tables 1, 2, 3).
It includes a narrative review of biophilic design in architecture and urban design (Section 2) and specific industrial design case studies (Section 3.1) to build its conceptual argument.
title: Biophilic Design and Bio-Collaboration: Applications and Implications in the Field of Industrial Design

limitations: Current examples of biophilic design in industrial products are relatively limited.
The conceptual framework for potential industrial design applications needs further definition through investigation.
Much development is still needed for bio-collaborative products to compete with prevailing unsustainable technologies.
The public needs to be educated and encouraged to participate in greening efforts.
Effective strategies to incorporate new understanding of natural systems within design education and practice need to be determined.
minimum_safe_summary: This paper proposes a conceptual framework for applying biophilic design, specifically 'bio-collaboration' with living organisms, to industrial design. It synthesizes existing research showing that biophilic environments in architecture and urban design improve human health, well-being, and productivity, and offers environmental benefits like pollution reduction and energy efficiency. The paper analyzes current industrial design examples that integrate living organisms for air purification, bio-manufacturing, and sustainable energy production, using both established biophilic attributes and newly proposed criteria for bio-collaboration. It concludes that bio-collaboration offers a promising sustainable design strategy, but acknowledges limitations such as the nascent stage of such products and the need for further framework development and multi-disciplinary collaboration.
